note: The same eight labelled changes at feature scale. Every other scene is identical between the drafts, so anything reported outside this set is a false positive.

changes.summary: The brass letter opener moves from scene 3 to scene 7.
changes.judgment: Same object relocated, not a cut and a new buy. Props needs the difference: a relocation is a continuity and set-dressing note, a new buy is a purchase order. The text supports identity: it is the same brass letter opener, and scene 7 says it sits 'where he left it'.
A rename, not a new role. Same scene, same function, identical dialogue. Casting must not be told to fill a new part; the existing booking carries over under a new name.

changes.summary: 'hands her the envelope' becomes 'slides the envelope across the table'.
changes.judgment: No props consequence: the envelope is unchanged and still one envelope. It is a different physical action and therefore a different camera setup, which is the AD's concern. This is the category a structural diff cannot resolve: the text changed, the kit did not.
Not a prop change at all. It is a scheduling change, and a possible location re-quote because a night shoot at a practical location is priced differently. Reporting this to props would be noise.
The scene number survives, which is why alignment still works. The county sheriff's office interior is no longer needed, and its content is largely absorbed by the new scene 5A.
A new exterior location (county office parking lot) and a picture vehicle. Transport is involved because the Bronco is a working vehicle in shot, not set dressing.

changes.summary: Wire-rimmed reading glasses are added in scene 7.
changes.judgment: A genuinely new item: it appears nowhere in draft 1. This is the contrast case for the letter opener, which looks similar to a diff but is not a new buy.

changes.summary: A Ford Bronco is named in the new scene 5A.
changes.judgment: A named brand introduced by the revision. Caught at script stage it is a phone call; caught after the shoot it is a reshoot. Transport also needs it because it is a picture vehicle.
